display: ML engineer in San Francisco working on recommendation ranking, curious about building feeds that are useful rather than just sticky.

signals.text: I'm tired of optimising click-through and want to work on a metric like 'that was useful' instead.
I'd like to find people who have tried measuring usefulness or satisfaction in ranking, not just engagement.
I'm leading a third iteration of a ranking model that is already at diminishing returns, and I could use fresh ideas.
I'm learning Mandarin to talk to my grandmother, and I'm stuck on things like yǒudiǎnr vs yìdiǎnr.
My grandmother speaks Hokkien and my own Mandarin is still robotic. I'd like to hear from anyone who has bridged a dialect gap with an older relative.
I've been stuck on a V6 climb called 'The Quiet One' for three weeks and am happy to swap beta.
I climb on weekends at Mission Cliffs and would enjoy a regular partner who talks honestly.
I'd like to be around work that feels less about capturing attention.
I'm lonely in a way I haven't said out loud. I put on a 'fine' face at work and with friends.
Layoff rumours at work and at competitors keep me anxious, and I wake around 4 a.m. most nights.
I'm sleeping about four hours a night and eating badly.
My housing costs are going up and I'm weighing whether to move.
I'd like to hear how others in the Bay Area have handled sudden rent increases in a small room.

offers.text: Three years building ranking and recommendation models with PyTorch and LightGBM.
I helped build a feature store, an offline evaluation harness and an A/B test pipeline, and I can talk through the design trade-offs.
I'm comfortable with Python, SQL and Spark, with some Rust.
I maintain a couple of small open-source tools on GitHub that others can use or extend.
I can explain how feed ranking works and what offline evaluation misses, in plain language, to non-ML people.
I can tell you what it's like to learn Mandarin from zero as an adult: a daily Anki routine with 1,100+ cards, 25 minutes on the BART, and a weekly tutor.
I have climbing gear and a Mission Cliffs membership, so I can bring a guest or introduce someone to bouldering.
I can listen when someone feels stuck, anxious or worn down. I know that feeling from the inside.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm starting a small project on recommenders that optimise for self-reported usefulness instead of clicks. I need someone who has run real ranking experiments.
catchers.can: Share how I'd design offline evaluation and A/B tests for a 'was this useful' metric, and sketch survey-based labels for ranking.
catchers.confirm: Is the project about ranking or recommendation quality with a non-click objective, rather than general content moderation or ad targeting?

catchers.hypo: I'm a researcher studying alternatives to engagement metrics in feeds. Do you have practical experience with offline evaluation harnesses?
catchers.can: Describe how our feature store, evaluation harness and A/B pipeline are structured, within what my employer allows me to share, and compare notes on pitfalls.
catchers.confirm: Do you want practitioner-level discussion of evaluation methodology rather than a full model audit or access to proprietary data?

catchers.hypo: I run a small open-source library for recommender evaluation and need a contributor who knows PyTorch, LightGBM and A/B testing.
catchers.can: Contribute small, well-scoped pull requests, and review design in the spare hours I have.
catchers.confirm: Is the contribution a small or part-time one that fits around a full-time job, rather than a full-time role?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Hokkien speaker from Penang (or the diaspora) and I'd like to practise with a younger person who wants to talk to their grandmother.
catchers.can: Introduce them to my grandmother Nai Nai for a short video call. She loves teasing my Mandarin. Via my mum, I can also translate between us.
catchers.confirm: Are you happy with a casual, language-practice conversation with an elderly relative in Penang, with my mum translating as needed?

catchers.hypo: I teach Mandarin to adult heritage learners who have family on the other side of a dialect gap. Do you know anyone who would benefit?
catchers.can: Join a learner group as a student and share my study routine, and pass along my tutor Wen's name if it's a fit.
catchers.confirm: Is the audience adult learners at beginner to lower-intermediate level who study a bit every day?

catchers.hypo: I'm trying to climb a V6 problem I keep falling off. Anyone at Mission Cliffs want to trade beta on Saturday?
catchers.can: Meet at Mission Cliffs on a weekend, share beta on 'The Quiet One', and pull a friend like Eli in as a third partner.
catchers.confirm: Is this a casual bouldering session at Mission Cliffs on a Saturday or Sunday around 10 a.m.?

catchers.hypo: My mum worries I don't eat properly while working long hours. I'd like to meet a young engineer who cooks simple food at home.
catchers.can: Compare notes on easy rice-based meals, and let my mum, who nags kindly about food, share recipes and suggestions.
catchers.confirm: Is this about practical home-cooking tips rather than diet plans or medical nutrition advice?

catchers.hypo: I work in tech and lost sleep over layoff rumours but haven't told anyone. Can I talk to someone who's been there?
catchers.can: Listen without advising, and share how I cope: climbing, a daily Mandarin routine, and a trusted friend who asks hard questions.
catchers.confirm: Do you want a peer to talk to rather than professional counselling or career advice?

catchers.hypo: I'm a manager who wants to be more honest with my team about uncertainty. What would help a person on my team?
catchers.can: Describe what direct, regular communication looks like from the receiving side, without naming my employer or my manager.
catchers.confirm: Is this a general conversation about communicating under uncertainty rather than a request about a specific company?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Bay Area tenant with a no-window room and a big rent increase. Does anyone know other rooms or local tenants' resources?
catchers.can: Share what I've learned from looking at Oakland and Bay Area room listings, and trade tips on tenant rights resources.
catchers.confirm: Is this about practical information on rooms and tenant resources rather than legal representation?

forbids.text: I can't take on unpaid work or anything that creates a gap in income.
I won't share my employer's proprietary models, data or internal metrics.
I'm not interested in work that is purely about increasing time-on-site or addictive engagement.
I can't commit to full-time extra work. My evenings and weekends are limited, and I'm at about 25 minutes of Mandarin practice every morning.
I'm not open to introductions that involve my family unless they're relevant and the family member agrees first.

projects.name: Usefulness-first ranking
projects.text: An exploration of recommenders that optimise for people saying 'that was useful' instead of clicks. It needs a metric, evaluation design, and a small group willing to test it.
roles_needed: product owner with a non-engagement goal

projects.name: Mandarin for Nai Nai
projects.text: A slow, personal project to learn enough Mandarin to hold a real conversation with my grandmother in Penang.

policy.t1: Give relevant technical background, my Mandarin and climbing interests, and specific ways I can help with ranking, evaluation or language practice.
policy.t2: Share candidly about work-related anxiety, sleep, finances and housing pressure, and equity, once I trust the person and know who they are.
policy.never: Never share resume or job-search plans, salary figures, immigration status, or my employer's confidential information.
